chunks: And Ibn Mahbub narrated from ʿAbd al-Wahhab ibn al-Sabbah, from ʿAli, from Abi Basir, from Abi ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, that he said:
Regarding a man who was struck in his ear and claimed that one of his ears had lost some of its hearing, he said:

“The one that was struck should be bound tightly and well, and the healthy one should be left open. Then a bell should be rung for him in front of his face, and he should be told: Listen. When the sound of the bell becomes hidden from him, its place is marked. Then the bell should be taken behind him and rung behind him until the sound becomes hidden from him; when it becomes hidden from him, its place is marked. Then the distance between the two is measured. If they are equal, it is known that he has spoken truthfully. Then it should be taken to his right and rung until it becomes hidden, then that is marked. Then it should be taken to his left and rung until it becomes hidden, then that is marked. Then the distance between the two is measured. If they are equal, it is known that he has spoken truthfully.”

He said: “Then his affected ear should be opened, and the other should be bound tightly and well. Then the bell should be rung in front of him, then its place should be marked until it becomes hidden. It should be done to him just as was done the first time with his healthy ear. Then the difference between the healthy ear and the affected ear is measured, and the compensation is assessed according to that.”

key_terms.أُذُنِهِ: his ear, the organ whose injury and hearing loss are being assessed
key_terms.سَمْعِهِ: his hearing, the faculty under legal examination
key_terms.فَيُقَوَّمُ: it is assessed/valued, meaning compensation is calculated accordingly
key_terms.يُقَاسُ: it is measured, indicating objective comparison in the procedure
key_terms.ٱلصَّحِيحَةِ: the healthy ear used as the comparative baseline
key_terms.ٱلْجَرَسِ: the bell used as the testing instrument for hearing
key_terms.ٱلْمُعْتَلَّةُ: the affected or impaired ear being evaluated

ai.seo_question: How is partial hearing loss assessed in Shia fiqh for legal compensation?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out a practical legal procedure for verifying a claimed loss of hearing after injury. It describes testing both the healthy and affected ear by measured sound distance, then determining compensation proportionate to the proven impairment.
